title: Clarify Segura2023 minor wurtzite indexing before accepting phase evidence
body:
# Clarify the minor wurtzite assignment in Segura et al. 2023 before using it as independent phase evidence

Source: Segura et al., *Sulfidogenic Bioreactor-Mediated Formation of ZnS Nanoparticles with Antimicrobial and Photocatalytic Activity*, Nanomaterials 13:935 (2023), DOI https://doi.org/10.3390/nano13050935.

The complete official 14-page PDF and Europe PMC XML were acquired. Pages 6–7/Figure 4 were checked directly. The predominant cubic ZnS assignment is separate from the question below; no incorrect alternative phase is asserted here.

The text assigns minor peaks at 34°, 36.2° and 47.6° 2θ to hexagonal (002), (101) and (102), respectively, while reporting a=0.3822 nm, c=0.6375 nm and wavelength=0.1541 nm. A consistency calculation using those same values yields approximately 27.98°, 30.41° and 39.22° for these planes. Figure 4 labels only the major cubic peaks; it does not resolve this text/cell/index discrepancy. The reported ICDD card also needs verification against the intended material and polymorph.

The round85 wurtzite owner therefore uses a separately inspected institutional primary experiment, Castillo Hernández's complete 2013 thesis Chapter 2. It does not count the 2023 article as accepted corroboration or transfer its photocatalytic/antimicrobial outcomes to pure wurtzite.

Acceptance conditions:

- Obtain an authoritative clarification, indexed diffraction data or correct reference-pattern documentation that reconciles peak positions, wavelength, unit cell and hkl labels.
- Determine whether the secondary phase is independently supported and whether any phase fraction can actually be estimated; do not infer purity from formula, XPS or average Scherrer size.
- Retain the predominant cubic product and mixed-phase nature. Keep microbial sulfide generation separate from phase-specific biological causation.
- If a record update becomes justified, cite exact corrected evidence, append EDIT history and obtain independent scientific review.

Evidence retained outside Git: `/private/tmp/cmm-round85-sulfides-research/zns2023.pdf` SHA256 `731e144c97dadb6580deffa83dcd79efff5170eb78829c9253bf3f0090cf289b`; XML SHA256 `10d784b650296bd9824e74713459afc159fb7569f2fd4501e32bdf09e5513349`; original page renders and `zns2023-phase-consistency.json`. The calculation is a curator consistency check, not a raw-data refinement. Current Crossref metadata has empty relation/update fields; a bounded DOI correction search found no resolving notice, which is not a universal absence claim. Full all-state issue inventory (285 entries) and hidden/ignored maintained roots were searched without a matching issue. Root should refresh live deduplication before posting.

title: Resolve zincite2020 dose and Zn balance inconsistencies before quantitative curation
body:
Resolve ZnO dose and Zn balance inconsistencies in Šebesta et al. (2020) before quantitative curation

The proposed zincite record retains a supported qualitative result: fungal-conditioned liquid partially converted zincite-structured ZnO nanoparticles into a mixed ZnO/zinc oxalate dihydrate solid. It deliberately does not accept a quantitative uptake or conversion efficiency.

Primary source: https://doi.org/10.3390/jof6040210 (complete 10-page original and official 6-page SI acquired).

Unresolved source questions:

- Main §2.2 states a common 6.5 mg Zn/L dose, but specifies 0.0033 g bulk ZnO in 50 mL. Using the Zn fraction of ZnO gives about 53 mg Zn/L; neither value should silently replace the other.
- Figure 2c labels the dissolved-fraction axis mg/L, with plotted means around 13–25 mg/L, above the stated 6.5 mg/L initial dose. The initial measured inventory, background Zn, concentration/dilution corrections and figure units need reconciliation before reuse of Figure 2 mass balance or the reported up-to-76% biomass allocation.
- The separate §2.3/3.2 metabolite assay reports 500 mg ZnO, 47.5 mL conditioned liquid plus 2.5 mL dispersion, oxalic acid 11.6→1.2 mmol/L and an inferred 43 mg/8.6% conversion. Resolve the concentration/volume basis and losses; this acid-consumption estimate is not a quantified XRD fraction or isolated-product yield. Figure 4 establishes coexistence of both phases, while the core-shell model remains proposed.

Acceptance: obtain a published correction, original deposited analytical/recipe data, or another legitimate primary clarification identifying actual feed amounts, measured initial and final Zn fractions, units/dilution factors, and the oxalate-based calculation. Verify against the original Figure 2/Figure 4 and SI; append canonical EDIT and independent successor review only if a maintained claim changes. Keep this issue open if the clarification is unavailable. No author contact is authorized or requested here.

Evidence retained outside Git:

- `/private/tmp/cmm-round85-phosphates-research/zincite2020-main.pdf`, SHA256 `0e57e247e141666ad937ee68ce704dbbc18e06b26e386b96f9f27b2930c7a454`; pages 3–6 and Figures2/4.
- `/private/tmp/cmm-round85-phosphates-research/zincite2020-si/jof-06-00210-s001.pdf`, SHA256 `2e24be842766e0bceaff123b99258564dbf113993ac0d607fa642b83188b90cb`; SI pp. 2–3 and Table S1/Figure S1 are the separate ionic-Zn preliminary assay.

All-state issue inventory checked with exact DOI/accession/material terms; matching issues: []. This is a bounded source-resolution gap, not a claim that no correction or data can exist elsewhere.

title: Clarify titanogypsum2021 loading, fluoride balance and mixed phase assignments
body:
Chen et al. (2021), *Red Yeast Improves the Potential Safe Utilization of Solid Waste (Phosphogypsum and Titanogypsum) Through Bioleaching*, [DOI10.3389/fbioe.2021.777957](https://doi.org/10.3389/fbioe.2021.777957), provides complete open primary evidence for a qualified titanogypsum record. The acquired13-page original, Table1, Figures1–7 and DataSheet1.docx (FiguresS1–S2) preserve several unresolved source ambiguities. This is a source clarification follow-up, not evidence that the narrowed record is incorrect.

Concrete work:

- Reconcile the abstract's g/mL loading statements with Methods (page3):5 or10g in150mL medium plus2mL inoculum. Do not infer corrected abstract units or a tolerance threshold.
- Recover an auditable fluorine balance across original waste, filtered liquid, cells, extracellular-polymer fraction and remaining solid, including dilution/fraction volumes, thermal preparation, polymer mass and analytical limits. Figure3B is the TG composition panel despite the prose citing3A; its relative elemental percentages and pyrolysis-loss panels are not whole-process recovery yields. Explain Table1's low sulfur relative to calcium in the source-labelled titanium gypsum.
- Obtain primary diffraction data/reference-card identities and clarify phase assignments in Figure4B, including signals in uninoculated arms. EDS colocalization and qualitative mixed XRD do not alone establish a phase-pure fluorophosphate product or exclusive microbial formation.
- Resolve repeated-label comparisons in the Results (including TG10-Rho compared with itself on page10) and supply the full Supplementary FigureS1 water-control recipe. FigureS2 concerns phosphogypsum and cannot substantiate titanogypsum fragmentation.
- Retain TG's lower filtered fluoride after inoculation, null phosphorus response and unmatched final pH. Stronger adsorption/biomineralization attribution requires discriminating controls; agricultural safety and deployment require direct evidence.

Acceptance requires a traceable correction, deposited data or other complete legitimate primary evidence that resolves these points. Add only supported claims to the maintained owner, append actual curation history if it changes, and obtain an independent exact-state scientific review. Do not substitute the phosphogypsum arm or source percentages with unresolved denominators. No author contact is requested.

Discovery duplicate check: round85's complete three-page all-state issue inventory (285items) and hidden/ignored/followed record/research/review/history search had no match for the normalized DOI or titanogypsum/titanium-gypsum identity. Root should repeat the live issue check before posting.

title: Resolve azurite2016 strain, phase-sample lineage and copper-removal recipe
body:
The new azurite record retains a qualified mixed-phase assignment from Kang et al. (2016), [DOI 10.2323/jgam.2016.03.001](https://doi.org/10.2323/jgam.2016.03.001). This is a source clarification task, not a known error in the scoped record.

The complete seven-page original was inspected. Figure 7 labels a small azurite contribution in a mixed pattern and identifies BPU medium; the separate copper-removal assay describes YA broth. The article calls the culture B-22/B22, but deposited KJ485701.1 currently labels S. soli B7-22. Original Methods print 5 microlitres inoculum, 2 mM copper and 48 h; Results use 2 M and extend the graph to 72 h. Figure 8's initial concentration also does not match 2 mM elemental copper.

Acceptance requires locating the specimen preparation and original diffraction data or an authoritative clarification, resolving strain/sample lineage, and reconciling the removal recipe and concentration basis. Preserve the narrower observation unless new evidence warrants correction. Do not convert 61.8% aqueous removal into an azurite yield or treat the external taxonomy species ID as strain authentication.

Original PDF SHA256: b6e7f94a43e8c29959b505cb320f11894bd37c1dcf4ba1db18f4c147d46c567c. The round85 source dossier retains acquisition and sequence evidence. Any later scientific change needs new history and a successor native review.

title: Clarify tenorite2021 thermal phase formation and mixed-product evidence
body:
The new tenorite record scopes the heated product of a fungal-conditioned preparation from Badawy et al. (2021), [DOI 10.3390/biology10030233](https://doi.org/10.3390/biology10030233). This is a source evidence follow-up, not a reason to claim direct living-cell CuO precipitation.

Methods 2.2 heats the collected precursor at 200°C for 24 h before characterization. No preheating diffraction or matched filtrate-free heated control separates fungal conditioning from thermal formation. The textual XRD angles conflict with Figure 1B and the stated 4–70° scan. Figure 4 assigns both Cu(I) and Cu(II); Figure 2 reports substantial sulfur in EDX. A phase-pure CuO product, isolated yield and copper reduction mechanism are therefore not established.

Acceptance requires original diffraction data and corrected peak assignments, pre/post-heating phase evidence and suitable abiotic controls, and clarification of residual sulfur and mixed oxidation-state interpretations. Retain source-assigned CuO as qualified evidence until these are resolved; do not promote a pure-product, microbial-necessity or industrial-recovery claim.

Complete 21-page original PDF SHA256: dcd840a3d531b9bffab16e4823ea4cc8a7ba473bf9da6e29aa434826c7813d31. Methods and Figures 1–4 were inspected; full XML and accession KY465752.1 are retained externally. Any later scientific edit needs new history and a successor native review.
